definitions.gloss: original text; original wording; the original
definitions.explanation: The text in its original form before translation, editing, or adaptation.

examples.japanese: {原文|げんぶん}を{確認|かくにん}する。
この{小説|しょうせつ}は{原文|げんぶん}で{読|よ}みたい。
examples.english: I want to read this novel in the original.

examples.japanese: {翻訳|ほんやく}は{良|よ}くできているが、{原文|げんぶん}のニュアンスとは{少|すこ}し{違|ちが}う。
examples.english: The translation is well done, but it differs slightly from the nuance of the original text.

notes:
Composed of {原|げん} (original/source) and {文|ぶん} (text/writing). Most commonly used when discussing translations, quotations, or edited works where comparison to the original is relevant.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {原文|げんぶん}で{読|よ}む: to read in the original language
- {原文|げんぶん}のまま: as it is in the original
- {原文|げんぶん}に{忠実|ちゅうじつ}: faithful to the original text
- {原文|げんぶん}を{引用|いんよう}する: to quote the original text

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {原作|げんさく}: original work — refers to the original creative work (novel, manga, etc.) that an adaptation is based on
- {原稿|げんこう}: manuscript, draft — a written document before publication
- {原典|げんてん}: original source — the primary source document, often academic
